outcome.answer:
LLM agents can reuse specific past workflows by storing prior interaction trajectories, abstracting them into reusable skills or procedural memories, and retrieving the most relevant ones for new tasks instead of reasoning from scratch each time [1, 3, 10]. LifeMem does this by clustering trajectories by underlying workflow, then recalling relevant skills and trajectories at inference time, which reduces forgetting and improves cross-task transfer [1]. TRIAGE similarly turns historical trajectories into reusable skills for direct reuse or parameter-substituted reuse on similar queries [10].

To avoid forgetting, the papers suggest that how memory is represented and organized matters as much as storing more experience [3]. Abstract procedural memories transfer more reliably than detailed trajectories, while some retrieval schemes can improve forward transfer yet still induce severe forgetting [3]. Structurally grouping related steps and dependencies into functional memory units or subgraphs can improve retention and retrieval of reusable procedures [7]. If the goal is to reuse workflow structures across tasks, SWIFT transfers structural priors and demonstrations from earlier workflow searches to synthesize new workflows without repeating search [2].
